title: Safe increment of the encoded index
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x,v$ be Boolean words, let $o$ be an oracle returning a Boolean answer for either of two indices on a Boolean word, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $v$ whose state is $s$. Suppose $i<|v|$ and every work-tape head of $c$ lies in $[-S,S]$. Starting the compiled program from the representation of $c$ with index $i$ in its increment phase, there is a finite number $T$ of steps after which it reaches the representation of $c$ with index $i+1$ in its query phase; every configuration strictly before that time satisfies the safety bounds for input length $|v|$ and space parameter $S$.
hypotheses_covered: A configuration $c$ on input $v$ with state equal to $s$
